newsitem.title: CHINA: SOCCER-DALIAN FIRE IN FIVE, STAY TOP CHINA LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DALIAN FIRE IN FIVE, STAY TOP CHINA LEAGUE.

text.p: China's northeastern soccer powerhouse Dalian Wanda crushed Beijing Guo'an 5-1 at home on Sunday, extending their lead in China's professional soccer league to 11 points.
The win, fired by goals from Wang Tao, Wang Peng and a hat-trick from Hao Haidong, extended Dalian's unbeaten streak in the league to 43 games, the Xinhua news agency said.
Two-time champion Dalian now tops the standings with 25 points, 11 points clear of 1995 champion Shanghai Shenhua, which drew 0-0 at home on Sunday against Guangzhou Apollo.
Dalian opened the scoring in the 15th minute with a volley by Wang Tao, but Beijing made it into the second half without further losses.
Hao opened his tally in the 67th minute and the game quickly turned into a rout as Beijing's defence crumbled under relentless assault from the home strikers.
Beijing, now fourth in the league with 13 points, scored their only goal in the 71st minute.
In the eastern city of Jinan, home side Jinan Taishan beat August First 1-0 on a second-half goal from Shao Yanjie, who converted a heading pass from Su Maozhen in the 70th minute.
In southern Guangzhou, Guangdong Hongyuan became the only home side loser on Sunday when it was beaten 3-2 by visiting Vanguard Huandao.
Hongyuan are now bottom in the league with only five points.
All the other matches ended in draws. Tianjin Samsung tied Sichuan Quanxing 1-1, while Qingdao Hainiu forced a goalless home draw with Yanbian Aodong.
